title: Across 35 gyre-density classes (sigma0 25.8-27.0, 1985-2021) the North Pacific outcrop-lightening law predicts AOU change only in the North Pacific and fails a pre-registered Southern Hemisphere test
abstract: Question: is the North Pacific (NP) law that links thermocline O2 loss to late-winter outcrop lightening (AOU profile shifted by kappa = 0.6 times the surface lightening) a general law? Approach: a plan locked before any change was calculated. We used GLODAPv2.2023 bottles (all oceans) for cell-matched AOU change (2006-2021 minus 1985-1999, cruise bootstrap) on 7 sigma0 classes (25.8-27.0) in 5 subtropical gyres (35 gyre-classes), and WOA23 decadal late-winter surface T and S for the class outcrop area change and the class surface density change (1995-2014 minus 1975-1994). The NP-calibrated law, without refit, gave predicted AOU changes. Main test: the 21 Southern Hemisphere (SH) gyre-classes. Results: the SH test failed. Predicted and observed SH changes had r = 0.16 (permutation p = 0.25), slope 0.37 (95% -0.34 to 0.93); outcrop area change had rho = -0.35 (p = 0.059). All 7 planned sensitivity runs agree (SH r 0.05-0.27, no slope interval excludes 0). Across all gyres r = 0.56 (slope 0.43), but without the NP r = 0.20 (p = 0.16). In the NP, open-ocean classes 25.8-26.6 follow the law (r = 0.98, slope 0.68; largest gain +10.7 umol/kg on 26.6, whose outcrop area fell 60%). The South Indian gyre gained 1.9-6.9 umol/kg AOU on all classes while its outcrop became slightly denser, and the North Atlantic gained 2-6 with small lightening; the South Atlantic lost 0.6-4.7 and became saltier on light isopycnals. Nitrate rose 0.11-0.16 per unit AOU in the NP, NA and SI, so these gains are oxygen use. Exploratory (post hoc): after we removed the part of AOU change that isopycnal salinity change predicts from the early spatial AOU-salinity slope, SH changes follow the law (r = 0.45, p = 0.023), so water-mass changes may hide a weak SH outcrop signal. Interpretation: the outcrop-lightening law is an NP law, not a global one. Projections that scale it with model surface lightening apply to the NP only. A parallel study (sci:3dd74f41) reached the same SH conclusion on 26.5 alone with a different surface metric; the two metrics disagree in sign in the South Indian gyre. Limitations: 10-17 cruises per SH epoch, two epochs, smoothed WOA23 decades with sparse early SH data, class bootstraps that ignore shared cruises (intervals too narrow), fixed kappa and lag, and a post hoc water-type correction with an unstable slope.
